Subject: Significant p95 jump after ModelPHI v2.1 rollout

Hi Mina / team,

We started seeing a sustained p95 increase across our production traffic shortly after the ModelPHI v2.1 rollout at ~12:30 UTC. Key metrics from our side: p95 increased from ~220ms to ~760ms, error rate ticked up to 0.6% (mostly 429/timeouts), and request queue length grew by ~3x on eu-west-1. This is impacting our customer chat flows.

We rolled a canary yesterday and had no issues — this looks like a scale interaction on higher concurrency. Can you tell us if there's an aggressive kernel selection or new batching behavior in v2.1 that could explain the tail?

Immediate ask: we need either (a) a rollback to the last stable variant (v2.0 quantized) or (b) a routing carveout so our traffic is pinned to the older variant while you investigate. We need a plan for the next 12 hours.

Logs and a heap sample attached.

Attachments: heap-sample-ops-0727.zip (sampled heap traces), brief metrics snippet included inline.

Thanks,
Olivia Barnes
Platform Ops — StellarTech
ops@stellartech.com

Subject: Re: Significant p95 jump after ModelPHI v2.1 rollout

Hi Olivia — thanks for the quick heads-up and for the heap sample. I copied SRE (Priyom) and CS (Dylan) so we can coordinate.

Quick summary of what we observed on Redwood: after the v2.1 rollout we saw a correlated increase in request batching depth for sequences < 128 tokens (kernel A switched to a different tiled path under specific load patterns). That path is more efficient for large batches but can elevate tail latency under high concurrency due to slower KV cache handoffs.

Immediate mitigations we've applied (in the last 20m):
- Traffic ramp-down: reduced incoming weight to ModelPHI v2.1 for StellarTech by 60%.
- Canary pin: pinned 10% to v2.0-quantized variant for comparison.
- Disabled auto-batcher for the affected routing pool (temporary).

Proposed next steps (need your authorization):
1) Authorized rollback to v2.0-quantized for StellarTech traffic only (target: 03:00 UTC to minimize user impact).
2) If rollback is not approved, we request permission for a temporary SLA carveout (p95 allowance to 1.0s) while we iterate on a code fix.
3) Post-mortem plan: we will run an expanded load matrix and push a patched v2.1.1 that reverts to the previous batching fallback behavior.

I've attached an SLO comparison and short incident report for your review.

Attachments: slo-report-2026-07-27.pdf

Let me know which option you prefer and whether you want an immediate rollback or the 03:00 UTC window.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
